params.body:
Closes #1097

## What went wrong

On 2026-11-14 a partner created a vehicle with photos through the partner API. For the third photo the bucket answered `503 Slow Down` to the HEAD in `VehicleApiService::addPhoto`, and again one second later. `VehicleApiController::store` rolled the whole vehicle back and the office got "kwam niet binnen via de API". It is the second vehicle lost to a short bucket hiccup in two weeks; #1059 covered the first, a timeout.

`StorageUnavailable::retryOnce` asks again after one second. That fits a timeout, where each attempt already waited fifteen seconds. A throttle answers at once and lifts within seconds, so both attempts fell inside the same window.

## What changes

- `StorageUnavailable::retryPastThrottle()`: `retryOnce()`, plus a third attempt four seconds later, taken only when the bucket itself answered 429 or 503 (`StorageUnavailable::throttled()` reads the status off the AWS exception in the chain). A timeout keeps its two attempts, so the slowest case is no slower than before.
- `addPhoto` uses it for the HEAD and for the three writes (1280, 1024 and 400 px).
- The three writes were bare `put()` calls on a disk that does not throw. The answers of the first two were not read, so a refused write left a row naming a file that was not in the bucket; a refused third one returned silently, so the vehicle was created with a photo missing and nobody was told. They now go through the Flysystem driver, which throws with the bucket's own answer: a write the bucket keeps refusing is a `StorageUnavailable`, and the existing rollback and office mail (cause: storage) take it from there.
- Rule R P3-2.7 says so.

The other callers of `retryOnce` (the sweepers, the upload job) are untouched: they have their own next run or queue retry.

## Cost

A partner call that meets a throttled bucket waits up to five seconds per storage call before it fails, instead of one. A healthy bucket sees the same four requests per photo as before.

## Tests

`APartnerPhotoWaitsOutAThrottledBucketTest` (7 cases) with an adapter that fails the way the S3 adapter does:

- a HEAD throttled twice lands on the third attempt, after pauses of 1 s and 4 s;
- a bucket that stays throttled is an error after three attempts, names the 503, leaves no row;
- a HEAD that times out gets two attempts, not three;
- a write throttled twice lands on the third attempt;
- a write the bucket keeps refusing is an error with no row, for each of the three sizes.

The existing partner-photo tests (`ASlowBucketIsNotAMissingPhotoTest`, `ImportedPhotosWithoutFileTest`, `PhotoRowOnlyWithFileTest`) pass unchanged. PHPStan reports no errors; pint passes on the added file.

The full suite ran once on this branch: 3266 tests, 33128 assertions, no failures (2 skipped, 1 incomplete).

## Not in this pull request

Why the bucket throttled at that moment is not known: it needs production figures (request rate against the bucket around 12:51 Brussels time on 2026-11-14). Who receives the office notice is #1098.
params.title: A partner's photo waits out a bucket that says slow down
